tagline: Yeast-based glabridin production inside engineered liquid-liquid phase-separated condensates, with success criteria written by industry
summary: Glabridin is 0.08-0.35% of licorice root dry weight and all three Glycyrrhiza species are on China's National Key Protected Wild Plants Catalogue, so one gram of the skincare active corresponds to roughly 286-1,250 g of dried root; GALATEA replaces that extraction route with Saccharomyces cerevisiae. The team built tunable protein condensates - an FTH1-24 ferritin iron core as nucleation seed, intrinsically disordered regions, and an SH3/PDZ scaffold at 3:1 recruiting the OC and DMT enzymes - instead of relying on random co-localisation. Their integrated human practices is organised as a four-act loop (Define, Optimize, Calibrate, Echo) in which each act must produce a change, and the loop closes by returning the engineering improvements to the same 96 street respondents for re-validation. Advice from Tsinghua chemical engineering professors reordered the biosynthetic pathway itself, and seven company visits rewrote the project's definition of success.

dry.frameworks: A six-module dry-lab pipeline run over four engineering rounds: M0 evidence collection, M1 sequence-level screening, M2 structural and assembly screening, M3 enzyme recruitment and partitioning, M4 pathway kinetics, M5 experimental comparison. Every module states explicitly what a negative screen does NOT establish (for example, 'M1 flags sequence and topology risks for structural follow-up; a negative screen does not establish enzyme activity or scaffold assembly'). Outputs were deliberately changed from a single yield prediction to 'recommended conditions + sensitivity ranking + uncertainty interval + failure criteria'.
dry.dataviz: A before/after paired bar chart of the same 96 street respondents' judgments; a stakeholder-by-theme emphasis matrix (eight engagement records x five themes, graded not highlighted / mentioned / discussed in depth); an interview coding grid (seven participants x five themes); consumer-needs and technical-concerns word clouds; a three-stage deployment-path diagram; and a two-column 'Measured Results / Next-Step Validations' format applied to every presentation slide.
dry.datascience: A 1,397-DOI literature analysis, a 16-compound computational safety screen against a fixed skincare reference panel, and a three-tier evidence table (Production, Skin Health, Safety) in which each entry records the experimental system, concentration range, source and evidence grade. Sequence screening uses IUPred2A disorder, SignalP, DeepTMHMM, PSIPRED, net charge per residue and mean hydropathy; all external data on the wiki carry source and experimental-condition labels, with literature values visually separated from the team's own measurements.
dry.software: GALATEA-Caelum, an integrated platform combining a literature-retrieval algorithm with an Agent harness that turns a researcher's prompt plus registered tools into a reviewable dry-lab plan grounded in the project's own wet-lab data. The retrieval algorithm queries OpenAlex, Crossref and Europe PMC, then ranks with BM25 (k1=1.5, b=0.75) plus BAAI/bge-m3 semantic embeddings, fuses with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, deduplicates by Jaccard, diversifies with MMR, rereads the full text of top records to extract numerical parameters, and runs AI-assisted quality evaluation. Built to be reused by future iGEM teams.
techniques: LLPS scaffold design with linker length and flexibility gradients
sensitivity ranking and uncertainty interval reporting

good.publicEngagement: Public engagement is built as a measurement instrument rather than a broadcast. Two rounds of street interviews (118 then 96 participants) bracket the engineering work: round one asked 'what do you need', round two revisited the same sites, gave respondents a short questionnaire, showed them the improved plain-language cards and the engineering evidence, then asked the same questions again - acceptance of biosynthetic ingredients rose 54.2% to 78.1%, the belief that a titre number alone is enough to judge success fell 71.9% to 22.9%, and willingness to pay 10% more for traceable production rose 26% to 51%. A 286-response campus questionnaire (18 items, two open-ended) plus 7 young-consumer interviews and 137 Q&A exchanges run with NUS supplied the baseline. Also four on-campus seminars (210 attendees), an offline outreach session at Beijing 101 High School, 23 articles on the WeChat account 'Tanwei iGEMer', two contributed pages in a science-outreach artbook with Rice iGEM, and the organisation of Tsinghua University's first Synthetic Biology Innovation Contest (62 teams from 21 universities).
good.ihp: GALATEA states its IHP function in one sentence - 'at each decision point it brings external stakeholders into the process and converts their judgment into concrete changes' - and then shows the conversions. The deepest chain runs through Professor Zheng Liu and Professor Chong Zhang of Tsinghua's Department of Chemical Engineering, who were shown the team's initial plan of directly fusing enzymes and relying on random co-localisation. They made three objections: random co-localisation cannot stop intermediates diffusing away before reaching the next enzyme; the DMT enzyme has high substrate promiscuity and poor selectivity, with a reported extracellular fraction of the intermediate demethylvestitol of 88.4 +/- 4.2%; and OC is hydrophobic, so it can be recruited into relatively hydrophobic droplets, and since OC is the rate-limiting step the OC:DMT ratio is the lever. The team changed four things: they replaced direct fusion with a tunable FTH1-24 ferritin-seeded scaffold plus IDR condensate and SH3/PDZ recruitment at 3:1 that keeps local OC concentration above DMT; they moved the DMT demethylation step to the very end of the biosynthetic pathway so promiscuity cannot contaminate intermediate steps; they expanded readouts from 'final yield only' to product identity, purity, intra- and extracellular intermediates, by-products, batch-to-batch stability and functional relevance; and they embedded red and green fluorescent markers in the scaffold so droplet formation and enzyme co-localisation are observed under the microscope rather than inferred. That is a stakeholder conversation changing the reaction order of a metabolic pathway. The seven company visits, sampled deliberately across supply-chain roles (Blue-Peptides and INNOBIO upstream in Dalian; WuXi Biologics and Zerun Biotech as CDMO in Shanghai; CHANDO Beauty Science City and Guyu Beauty as end brands in Guangzhou; IMEIK against medical-device standards in Beijing), were run with the same four questions each time, and each produced a specific change: Blue-Peptides' line that 'an unrepeatable yield figure equals zero in industry' added a batch-to-batch variation column to the experimental records; WuXi Biologics' thresholds of purity >= 95% and +/- 5% batch variation went into the wet-lab detection items; CHANDO's raw-material gate (efficacy, safety, cost and supply stability all must pass) and Guyu's four-document procurement logic split efficacy evidence into in vitro cellular and formulation tiers so in vitro results are never presented as efficacy claims; IMEIK's insistence that a complete data package matters more than any single impressive metric produced a data-package checklist consolidating all seven companies' requirements with a tick-box for whether the team currently holds each item. Together these rewrote the judgment chain from 'LLPS works -> leakage falls -> yield rises -> success' to that chain plus product identity and quality evidence plus functional relevance to specific skin problems. NUS professors' critique that partition coefficient, leakage rate, linker flexibility and effective enzyme concentration were implicit and invisible drove the model-output change and the three-tier evidence table. Peer iGEM teams each closed a specific gap: Nanjing Normal University on genomic integration versus plasmid expression to reduce batch variation; Nankai University on platform scope and the scale-up bottleneck, which the team admits they could not answer at the time and then added to the public project description; Beijing Institute of Technology on provenance, pointing out that an unlabelled 88.4% leakage figure would read as the team's own measurement - which is why every external number on the wiki now carries a source label. Conference feedback was treated the same way: NCIM made them split every slide into 'Measured Results' and 'Next-Step Validations'; CCiC's objection that a single leakage percentage without a stated loading ratio is meaningless added the three comparison groups (free enzyme, random co-localisation, LLPS scaffold) and the 1:1 / 1:2 / 2:1 recruitment gradient to the formal protocol; APiC moved the fluorescence co-localisation data out of the appendix and into results; and a question at the Peking-Rice Summit about skin-tone controversy produced the impact-boundary assessment. They also adopted Beijing Institute of Technology's HP process discipline - preparation, execution, review, with a named note-taker per phase - so every visit produced minutes in a fixed format.
good.realWorld: The need is quantified at the resource level: 0.08-0.35% glabridin content in licorice root, all three Glycyrrhiza species protected under Chinese law, 286-1,250 g of dried Uzbek root and stolon per gram of product assuming complete recovery, and documented habitat degradation from overharvesting. Only three SDGs are claimed - 3 Good Health and Well-being, 9 Industry Innovation and Infrastructure, 12 Responsible Consumption and Production - and each is tied to a specific question (what makes the ingredient useful, how it should be produced, how materials are used responsibly). Crucially, the sustainability page contains a table mapping each HP concern to its source participant or specialist, to the assessment dimension it created, to what was actually included in the analysis, and to the SDG connection, so the SDG link is derived from stakeholder evidence rather than asserted. The regulatory path is checked item by item against Chinese cosmetic law: spot-fading and whitening claims require human efficacy evaluation trials, naming follows the Cosmetic Classification Rules and Catalogue, biotechnological raw materials fall under YY/T 10001-2026, and new ingredients require registration and filing - from which the team concludes that efficacy claims are their most constrained category because their evidence stops at the in vitro and yeast level, far below what the claim would require. A negative-impacts table lists who is affected, under what conditions, the residual uncertainty and the team's own boundary for three topics including colorism, committing to never rank skin tones by lightness and to use specific skin-problem wording instead. Deployment is staged with a cost target: 1-2 years to prove platform portability to other high-value molecules, 2-3 years to pilot-scale fermentation with dry-lab models recalibrated against the industrial parameters collected on the visits, aiming to bring cost from about RMB 100,000 per kilogram at lab scale to below RMB 30,000, then 3-5 years into cosmetics, traditional Chinese medicine and nutraceuticals via licensing and joint development. Most tellingly, the one thing public communication could not fix is reported unfixed: 56.3% still regarded price as a major barrier after seeing the cards, so the team wrote price back into the Part 3 cost targets 'unchanged' and added 'efficacy claims running ahead of evidence' to its red lines for future communication.

gemsTakeaway: Close the loop by measuring it: take the engineering changes stakeholder feedback produced back to the same respondents, ask the same questions before and after, and publish the one metric that did not move - then convert industry's hard thresholds into the project's own definition of a successful design, so a higher titre alone can no longer count as success.
